svg.title: What the Mamba2 bottleneck layer does
svg.desc: Three panels. One: the 5 by 9 by 9 bottleneck grid with 320 channels is flattened into a sequence of 405 tokens. Two: the Mamba2 scan. Reading the tokens in order, a fixed-size state is carried from token to token. At each token the old state is scaled by a factor a between 0 and 1 (forget), the token is written in through B, and an output is read from the state through C. The factors are computed from each token, so the layer chooses what to remember. The cost grows linearly with the number of tokens. Three: the layer's steps in U-Mamba2: LayerNorm, a linear layer from 320 to 640 channels plus a gate, B, C and step size, a short convolution over 4 tokens, the scan with 8 heads of 80 channels and state size 32, gating and RMSNorm, and a linear layer back to 320 channels, reshaped to 5 by 9 by 9.
svg.text: 1 · FLATTEN THE BOTTLENECK INTO A SEQUENCE
405 tokens, each a vector of 320 numbers
The Mamba2 layer reads them in order,
2 · THE SCAN: ONE PASS OVER THE TOKENS, CARRYING A SMALL STATE
at (between 0 and 1): how much of the old
state to keep. Bt: how to write the token in.
All three are computed from xt itself, so the
layer decides token by token what to remember.
The state has a fixed size, so the cost grows linearly with the number of tokens. Attention would compare every pair: 405 × 405.
In Mamba2, at is a single number per head. That simpler form lets the scan be computed in parallel as matrix multiplications.
Simplified: the equations leave out the step size Δ and a direct skip term D · x, which Mamba2 also uses.
